slides.title: Duolingo FY2025 investor update
slides.subtitle: Results and 2026 plan, from public filings · Illustrative example, not affiliated with Duolingo
slides.notes: Built only from the FY2025 10-K and the Q4 FY2025 / Q4 FY2024 shareholder letters.

slides.title: Duolingo is trading 2026 bookings growth for user growth, so judge 2026 by DAUs
points: 2025 delivered scale and profit: revenue rose 39% to $1.04B and adjusted EBITDA margin reached 29.5%
User growth slowed: DAU growth fell from 51% to 30% and paid subscriber growth from 43% to 28%
The 2026 plan gives up about 5 points of bookings growth and accepts lower margins to grow users faster
$360M of free cash flow and $1.04B in cash can fund that bet and a $400M buyback
slides.notes: The answer first; the rest is proof.

slides.title: Revenue grew 39% to $1.04B in 2025, the first year above $1B

evidence: E1 Revenue FY2023: $531.1M (earlier years lower: FY2020 $161.7M, FY2021 $250.8M, FY2022 $369.5M) [SRC 1]
E4 Revenue growth: FY2024 40.8%, FY2025 38.7% (letters round to 41% and 39%) [CALC]

slides.notes: Growth was 41% in 2024 and 39% in 2025; the top line barely slowed.

slides.title: Operating margin rose from 8.4% to 13.1%, and adjusted EBITDA margin reached 29.5%

ghost.exhibit: bar — operating margin FY2023-FY2025, % (adjusted EBITDA margin FY2024-FY2025 in the takeaways)
evidence: E7 Adjusted EBITDA FY2024 $191.9M (25.7% margin); FY2025 $305.9M (29.5%) — non-GAAP [SRC 2]

slides.notes: Adjusted EBITDA is non-GAAP; say so on the slide.

slides.title: A one-time $257M tax benefit makes up most of 2025's $414M net income

ghost.exhibit: stacked bar — FY2025 net income split: one-time tax benefit vs the rest, $M
evidence: E9 One-time income-tax benefit 2025 from valuation allowance release: $256.7M [SRC 2]
E10 Share of FY2025 net income from the one-time benefit: 62%; remainder about $157.4M [CALC]

slides.notes: The rest is about $157M by simple subtraction; this is not a company-reported figure.

slides.title: User growth slowed in 2025: DAUs grew 30% after 51%, and MAUs 14% after 32%

ghost.exhibit: highlight table — YoY growth of DAUs, MAUs, paid subscribers, Q4 2024 vs Q4 2025, %

slides.notes: This is the complication: the engine behind revenue is slowing.

slides.title: Engagement still deepened: 40% of monthly users now open the app daily, up from 35%

ghost.exhibit: bar — DAU/MAU ratio, Q4 2024 vs Q4 2025, %

slides.notes: Fewer new users, but the ones who stay use it more.

slides.title: Paid subscribers grew 28% to 12.2M, slower than the 43% of a year earlier

ghost.exhibit: bar — paid subscribers Q4 2024 vs Q4 2025, M, with share of MAUs
evidence: E15 Paid subscribers / MAUs: Q4 2024 8.1%; Q4 2025 9.2% [CALC]

slides.notes: Paid share of MAUs rose from 8.1% to 9.2%; monetization of the base is still improving.

slides.title: 2026 guidance cuts bookings growth to 10-12% by giving up over $50M of bookings to grow free users

ghost.exhibit: bar — total bookings growth FY2024, FY2025, FY2026 guidance midpoint, %
evidence: E17 2026 guidance: bookings $1,274-1,298M (+10% to +12%); revenue $1,197-1,221M (+15% to +18%); adjusted EBITDA margin 25.0% [SRC 2]
E18 Management estimate: more than $50M of foregone bookings, about 5 points of growth, invested in the free user experience [SRC 2]

slides.notes: Management's estimate: about 5 points of growth deliberately foregone.

slides.title: Margins step down in 2026: gross margin to about 69% on AI costs, adjusted EBITDA margin to 25%

ghost.exhibit: line — gross margin FY2023-FY2025 and 2026 guidance, %
evidence: E17 2026 guidance: bookings $1,274-1,298M (+10% to +12%); revenue $1,197-1,221M (+15% to +18%); adjusted EBITDA margin 25.0% [SRC 2]
E19 Gross margin FY2023 73.2%, FY2024 72.8%, FY2025 72.2% [CALC]
E20 Gross margin guidance: about 71% in Q1 2026, roughly 69% for the rest of 2026, mainly from AI features for all users [SRC 2]

slides.notes: Guidance, not results; AI features for all users drive the gross-margin step-down.

slides.title: $360M of free cash flow and $1.04B in cash can fund the user bet and a $400M buyback

ghost.exhibit: bar — operating cash flow and free cash flow FY2024-FY2025, $M; cash at year end in takeaways
evidence: E21 Free cash flow FY2024 $264.4M; FY2025 $360.4M (+36%) — non-GAAP [SRC 2]
E24 Operating cash flow FY2024 $285.5M; FY2025 $387.8M [SRC 1]

slides.notes: Free cash flow is non-GAAP. The buyback is an authorization; timing is discretionary.

slides.title: Judge 2026 by whether DAU growth re-accelerates above 2025's 30%, not by bookings growth
